# Lepons

> Lepons is a free, open-source (MIT) desktop app (Windows, macOS) that puts the AI coding agents on all your PCs on one screen: Claude Code, Codex, Grok, Antigravity, Cursor and OpenCode, on this PC and on any VM or server it reaches over SSH. A model on your own server (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM) or behind an API key (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Groq) runs in OpenCode; keys stay encrypted on your own PC. It shares codebases between computers, draws all the work on one workflow map, splits the screen into panes with tabs, and has a phone app to carry on while away.

- Home (Korean): https://lepons.app/
- Home (English): https://lepons.app/en/
- Download (Windows .exe, macOS .dmg): https://github.com/joyuno/lepons/releases/latest
- Source code (MIT License): https://github.com/joyuno/lepons
- Android APK: https://github.com/joyuno/lepons/releases/latest/download/Lepons-Android.apk
- Guide (Korean): https://github.com/joyuno/lepons/blob/main/README.md
- Guide (English): https://github.com/joyuno/lepons/blob/main/README.en.md
- Privacy: https://lepons.app/privacy
- Terms: https://lepons.app/terms
- Support: https://lepons.app/support

## Key facts
- Sharing map: drag a folder onto another computer and its agents read and search it over MCP (read-only, values that look like secrets are masked). Work can be delegated to the computer that owns the folder; delegated work runs without permission prompts, so share only between computers you trust. It is meant for closed company networks, files that should not go to GitHub, and anyone who would rather not commit, push and pull (or is new to git): git moves files but not the conversation, while here the other computer's AI reads only the files it needs, in place, saving the round trip and tokens.
- Workflow map (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+M): each computer branches into folders, sessions and subagents, with always-visible summaries and a Goal / Progress / Now / Result card per session. "Needs you N" steps through waiting sessions. The map is for watching; answers go in the session's pane.
- Panes: up to eight on screen. A pane holds one project's AI sessions, terminals and files as tabs. Files on this PC or a remote machine can be viewed and edited in place.
- Remote machines need only SSH; nothing from Lepons is installed there. With tmux, sessions survive dropped connections. If tmux is missing, Lepons installs it in one click (a sudo password is asked in its own dialog and never saved).
- AI sign-ins: see each computer's AI install and sign-in state, install what is missing (OpenCode included), and sign in on remote machines, with no terminal commands to start.
- Phone app: Android as a direct APK (Google Play is a closed test); iPhone on the App Store (https://apps.apple.com/app/id6829282468). Pairs by QR plus a six-digit check, signs in with a password and an authenticator (TOTP) code, and connects through a relay (relay.lepons.app) with end-to-end encryption the relay cannot read. From the phone: see every session's state, answer an AI's choices or type a reply, open, close and reconnect sessions, attach photos and files, open the PC's terminal, browse folders with images, highlighted code and HTML pages, follow the workflow map, and check usage. Notifications come when an AI puts up a choice or stops on an error or a usage limit, carrying the folder, AI and PC names and one fixed line. One PC connects to one phone; one phone can keep several PCs paired and switch between them, and a notification from another PC switches to it.
- Usage: the last 7 days by project and model, from this PC and from remote PCs over SSH (only counts are read, never conversations).
- Korean-first (English and Chinese too); AI installs, sign-ins, remote PCs and phone pairing are done through buttons and guides, so non-developers rarely need a terminal.
- Free, no Lepons account, no ads. The PC app needs each AI tool's own account.
